market_story: coal / gas ST: a unit that is dead does not clear, and a unit that is alive does. Sherco-2 (682 MW), Karn 1-2 (486 MW), A B Brown 1+2 (485 MW), Petersburg-ST2 (422 MW), SOC 5+6 (496 MW) really ran through 2023 — 7.7 TWh of measured generation — and left the market on published EIA-860 retirement months their surviving plants outlived. The fleet snapshot had erased them wholesale (so 2023 under-carried coal by ~8 TWh), and the miso-190 repair attempt resurrected them without their death dates (so 2024/2025 over-carried by ~10 TWh/yr). The exit-cohort bins carry each unit exactly as the market did: in merit while it existed, gone from the month EIA records its exit, its still-running siblings (Sherco 1+3, SOC 7+8) untouched. Big Cajun 2-1 and Warrick-2 — snapshot-mothballed but OP in the year-matched vintage — re-enter at their vintage ratings for exactly the years the record says they operated. No offer, floor or price parameter moves; the change is fleet membership and exit timing on EIA's own published records.
